issues.title: rebalancer: Restore missing `slippage_predictor.rs` implementation to fix broken builds
issues.body:
`contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/slippage_predictor.rs` was emptied out to 0 bytes in commit `f4090c336d6e5022033f593f33ee5d9b82794e1e` ("closed").

Meanwhile, `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/lib.rs` continues to declare:
```rust
mod slippage_predictor;
use slippage_predictor::predict_slippage;
```
and invokes `predict_slippage(trade.asset_pair.clone(), trade.amount, &env)` on every trade inside `MultiAssetRebalancer::rebalance`.

## Why this matters

Because `slippage_predictor.rs` is completely empty, any build or test referencing `rebalancer-contract` will fail with an unresolved import error. Furthermore, `.kiro/specs/rebalancer-slippage-predictor/FINAL_COMPLETION_REPORT.md` documents an entire completed specification for constant-product / liquidity-based slippage calculations that was inadvertently lost or deleted. Without this module, rebalancing trades cannot estimate price impact or compute slippage protection.

## Tasks

- [ ] Re-implement `predict_slippage` in `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/slippage_predictor.rs` conforming to the signature `pub fn predict_slippage(asset_pair: (Symbol, Symbol), amount: u128, env: &Env) -> U256`
- [ ] Ensure non-zero trade sizes against thin liquidity estimate higher slippage than against deep liquidity
- [ ] Handle zero amounts and unknown pairs gracefully without panicking
- [ ] Add unit tests in `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/tests.rs` covering small, large, and zero-liquidity scenarios
- [ ] Verify that `cargo test -p rebalancer-contract` passes

## Files to look at

- `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/slippage_predictor.rs`
- `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `.kiro/specs/rebalancer-slippage-predictor/design.md`
- `.kiro/specs/rebalancer-slippage-predictor/FINAL_COMPLETION_REPORT.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- `rebalancer-contract` compiles cleanly without unresolved symbol errors
- `predict_slippage` returns dynamic slippage values matching trade size and pair depth
- All unit tests pass in CI

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban, DeFi mechanics  
**Estimated effort:** 1 day

issues.title: treasury: Implement on-chain Stellar Asset Contract (SAC) token transfers for deposits and payouts
issues.body:
In `contracts/treasury-contract/src/lib.rs`, the methods `deposit`, `withdraw`, `emergency_withdraw`, and `distribute_reward` currently only increment and decrement internal integers in contract instance storage (`(BALANCE, category)`):

```rust
let balance: i128 = env.storage().instance().get(&key).unwrap_or(0);
let new_balance = balance.checked_add(amount).ok_or(Error::Overflow)?;
env.storage().instance().set(&key, &new_balance);
```

The contract never invokes `soroban_sdk::token::Client::new(&env, &token).transfer(...)` to pull tokens from donors during deposit, or send tokens to recipients during withdrawal and reward distribution.

## Why this matters

`TreasuryContract` is described in the README as the "financial heart of Trellis, managing protocol funds". Currently, it manages phantom ledger numbers: it holds zero real SAC tokens, and calls to `withdraw` or `distribute_reward` emit success events while zero tokens actually move on the Stellar ledger.

## Tasks

- [ ] Bind an accepted token address (or token whitelist) to `TreasuryContract` during initialization
- [ ] In `deposit`, call `token::Client::transfer(&donor, &contract_address, &amount)` after validating caller auth
- [ ] In `withdraw` and `emergency_withdraw`, execute `token::Client::transfer(&contract_address, &to, &amount)`
- [ ] In `distribute_reward`, execute `token::Client::transfer(&contract_address, &recipient, &amount)`
- [ ] Ensure checks-effects-interactions order is preserved (storage decremented before external token transfer)
- [ ] Update `contracts/treasury-contract/src/test.rs` to verify real token balances via `env.register_stellar_asset_contract`

## Files to look at

- `contracts/treasury-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/treasury-contract/src/test.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs` (as reference for `token::Client` usage)

## Acceptance criteria

- Deposits transfer actual SAC tokens from the caller into the treasury contract
- Withdrawals and reward distributions transfer SAC tokens from treasury to target recipients
- Tests assert token balances alongside internal category balances

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Token SDK  
**Estimated effort:** 2–3 days

issues.title: aid-contract: Eliminate unbounded `KEY_AIDS` map in `create_aid` causing storage and gas exhaustion
issues.body:
In `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs` (lines 261–267), each call to `create_aid` performs:

```rust
let mut aids: Map<u64, AidRecord> = env
    .storage()
    .persistent()
    .get(&KEY_AIDS)
    .unwrap_or_else(|| Map::new(&env));
aids.set(aid_id, record);
env.storage().persistent().set(&KEY_AIDS, &aids);
```

This is done in addition to storing the record individually under `set_aid(&env, aid_id, &record)` on line 259.

## Why this matters

Soroban enforces a maximum entry size limit on persistent storage items (typically 64 KB). Because `KEY_AIDS` stores a single serialized `Map<u64, AidRecord>`, after approximately 300–400 aid records are created, `KEY_AIDS` will exceed the maximum storage entry size and cause every subsequent `create_aid` call to panic and fail. Furthermore, deserializing and re-serializing an unbounded map on every single aid creation causes `O(N)` CPU and RAM gas consumption.

## Tasks

- [ ] Remove `KEY_AIDS` unbounded map from `create_aid`
- [ ] Rely solely on individual persistent keys `DataKey::Aid(aid_id)` (already wrapped by `set_aid` and `get_aid`)
- [ ] If collection indexing is needed for pagination, store bounded chunk indices or cursor ranges rather than a single monolithic map
- [ ] Add a stress test in `contracts/aid-contract/src/tests.rs` simulating hundreds of aid creations without entry size bloat

## Files to look at

- `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/storage.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/tests.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- `create_aid` operates in `O(1)` storage operations regardless of how many aids have been created
- Storage entry size for any single key never grows unbounded with aid volume
- All existing aid tests continue to pass

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Storage Architecture  
**Estimated effort:** 1–2 days

issues.title: aid-contract: Fix inverted error code in `create_aid` and enforce caller auth in `refund_aid`
issues.body:
In `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs`, there are two logic and authorization defects:

1. **Inverted error code in `create_aid` (line 217):**
```rust
if expiry_ledger <= env.ledger().sequence() {
    env.panic_with_error(AidError::NotExpiredYet);
}
```
When a donor passes an expiry ledger that has already occurred or is current, the contract panics with `NotExpiredYet` instead of `Expired` or `InvalidArgument`.

2. **Missing caller authentication in `refund_aid` (lines 356–387):**
The documentation on line 358 states: `/// Only the donor or the admin may trigger the refund.` However, `refund_aid` contains no `donor.require_auth()` or `admin.require_auth()`. Any external unauthenticated account can invoke `refund_aid` as soon as the expiry ledger passes.

## Why this matters

- Returning `NotExpiredYet` when an expiry has already elapsed creates confusing error diagnostics for integrators and frontends.
- Unauthenticated refunds allow front-running or griefing of refund workflows without donor coordination.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `create_aid`, replace `AidError::NotExpiredYet` with `AidError::Expired` when `expiry_ledger <= env.ledger().sequence()`
- [ ] In `refund_aid`, require authorization from either `record.donor` or the contract admin (`caller.require_auth()`)
- [ ] Add negative unit tests in `contracts/aid-contract/src/tests.rs` verifying that unauthenticated callers cannot trigger `refund_aid`
- [ ] Add test verifying that past expiry ledgers in `create_aid` return `AidError::Expired`

## Files to look at

- `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/errors.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/tests.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- `create_aid` panics with `AidError::Expired` if `expiry_ledger <= env.ledger().sequence()`
- `refund_aid` enforces that only the donor or admin can execute the refund
- Unit tests cover all unauthorized and invalid expiry paths

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Auth  
**Estimated effort:** 4 hours

issues.title: referral: Migrate referral edges, user balances, and caps from instance to persistent storage
issues.body:
In `contracts/referral-contract/src/lib.rs`, referral relationships and balances are stored directly in `instance` storage:

```rust
// Line 295:
env.storage().instance().set(&DataKey::Referrer(wallet.clone()), &referrer);

// Line 416:
env.storage().instance().set(&DataKey::Accrued(referrer.clone()), &0_i128);
```

Similarly, `LifetimeAccrued` is written to instance storage.

## Why this matters

According to `shared/src/storage.rs` guidance:
> "Contract config (admin, token…) -> instance"
> "Referral edges & accrued balances -> persistent (Per-address data that outlives a single transaction)"

Soroban instance storage has a strict size limit of 64 KB across all entries. Storing every user's referrer address, accrued commission balance, and lifetime earnings in instance storage means the contract will fail and halt all new referral registrations as soon as user count grows.

## Tasks

- [ ] Migrate `DataKey::Referrer(Address)` from `env.storage().instance()` to `env.storage().persistent()`
- [ ] Migrate `DataKey::Accrued(Address)` and `DataKey::LifetimeAccrued(Address)` to `persistent()` storage
- [ ] Use `shared::storage::persistent_get` and `persistent_set` with TTL extensions (`PERSISTENT_BUMP_AMOUNT`)
- [ ] Ensure `claim_rewards`, `accrue`, and `register` handle persistent storage reads and updates
- [ ] Verify test suite in `contracts/referral-contract/src/lib.rs` passes with persistent keys

## Files to look at

- `contracts/referral-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `shared/src/storage.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- User-specific referral data is stored in persistent storage with automatic TTL bumps
- Instance storage is reserved strictly for contract-wide config (admin, max_tiers, reward_cap, treasury)
- Registration of large volumes of users does not bloat instance storage

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Storage Architecture  
**Estimated effort:** 1–2 days

issues.title: access-control: Refactor monolithic `RoleMembers` map to composite storage keys
issues.body:
In `contracts/access-control/src/lib.rs` (lines 72–73), role membership is stored as:

```rust
/// Members of a role: `role -> Map<Address, bool>`.
RoleMembers(Symbol),
```

Whenever a role is granted, revoked, or queried, the entire `Map<Address, bool>` for that role is fetched from storage, deserialized, modified, and reserialized.

## Why this matters

For protocol-wide roles like `beneficiary`, `donor`, or `manager` that can scale to thousands of addresses, holding all members inside a single `Map` will quickly exceed the maximum persistent entry size limit (64 KB) and transaction memory limits. Once full, no new members can ever be granted that role.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace `DataKey::RoleMembers(Symbol)` with a composite key: `DataKey::RoleMember(Symbol, Address)` storing `bool`
- [ ] Update `grant_role`, `revoke_role`, and `has_role` to perform direct `O(1)` key lookups
- [ ] Maintain an optional role member counter or paginated member index if member enumeration is required
- [ ] Update all unit tests in `contracts/access-control/src/lib.rs`

## Files to look at

- `contracts/access-control/src/lib.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Checking or modifying role membership executes in `O(1)` storage operations
- Role member storage scales indefinitely without hitting entry size thresholds
- All RBAC hierarchy tests remain green

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Storage Optimization  
**Estimated effort:** 1 day

issues.title: registry: Store contracts and metadata under individual persistent keys instead of monolithic maps
issues.body:
In `contracts/registry-contract/src/lib.rs` (lines 110–145), the registry contract stores all registrations and version histories in three global `Map`s in instance storage:

```rust
const KEY_CONTRACTS: Symbol = symbol_short!("contracts"); // Map<Symbol, ContractRegistration>
const KEY_METADATA: Symbol = symbol_short!("metadata");   // Map<Symbol, MetadataEntry>
const KEY_HISTORY: Symbol = symbol_short!("history");     // Map<Symbol, Vec<u32>>
```

## Why this matters

Instance storage is capped at 64 KB and shares the lifecycle of the contract instance. Storing strings, IPFS URIs, SHA-256 byte arrays, and version arrays for every contract in the Trellis ecosystem in instance maps will cause the contract to exceed instance storage quota as modules and metadata evolve.

## Tasks

- [ ] Refactor contract registration storage to use individual keys: `DataKey::Contract(Symbol)`
- [ ] Refactor metadata storage to use `DataKey::Metadata(Symbol)`
- [ ] Store historical version records under `DataKey::VersionHistory(Symbol, u32)` or individual version entries
- [ ] Migrate long-term metadata to persistent storage with TTL management
- [ ] Retain lightweight directory indexing in instance storage if needed for enumeration

## Files to look at

- `contracts/registry-contract/src/lib.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Registering new contracts and metadata does not deserialize unrelated contracts
- Instance storage consumption remains small and bounded
- `get_contract`, `get_metadata`, and `get_version_history` function with full backward compatibility

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Architecture  
**Estimated effort:** 1–2 days

issues.title: governance: Bridge multi-sig parameter execution to target contracts via cross-contract calls
issues.body:
In `contracts/governance-contract/src/lib.rs` (lines 576–600), when a multi-sig proposal executes `ProposalAction::SetParameter(key, value)`:

```rust
ProposalAction::SetParameter(key, value) => {
    validate_param(key, *value)?;
    write_param(env, key, *value);
}
```

It updates only `GovernanceContract`'s local instance storage (`write_param`). It never invokes cross-contract calls on the target contracts whose parameters it supposedly controls.

## Why this matters

`AidContract`, `TreasuryContract`, and `ReferralContract` each maintain their own independent configuration and never query `GovernanceContract`. As a result, approved multi-sig governance proposals to adjust treasury limits, aid expiry, or referral tier basis points have zero effect on the actual running contracts.

## Tasks

- [ ] Integrate `RegistryContract` resolution in `GovernanceContract` to look up live contract addresses
- [ ] In `execute_action` for `ProposalAction::SetParameter`, invoke the corresponding contract entry point:
  - `AidDefaultExpiry` -> `AidContract::update_config`
  - `TreasuryWithdrawalLimit` -> `TreasuryContract::set_withdrawal_limit`
  - `ReferralTierBps` / `ReferralRewardCap` -> `ReferralContract::set_tier_config`
- [ ] Add cross-contract client mocks and integration test in `shared/tests/integration.rs` verifying that executing a governance proposal modifies target contract state

## Files to look at

- `contracts/governance-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/treasury-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/referral-contract/src/lib.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Executing a multi-sig parameter proposal updates the target contract's active parameters
- Unauthorized or failing target calls roll back the proposal execution atomically
- End-to-end integration test passes in CI

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Cross-Contract Invocations  
**Estimated effort:** 3–5 days

issues.title: upgradeability: Enforce mandatory timelock delay for non-emergency contract upgrades
issues.body:
In `contracts/upgradeability/src/lib.rs`, `UpgradeProposal` is created via `propose_upgrade` and can be immediately executed via `execute_upgrade` by an account holding the `Upgrader` role within the same transaction or block.

There is no timelock, grace period, or scheduling delay enforced between proposal creation and execution.

## Why this matters

Smart contracts that escrow aid funds and treasury reserves cannot safely allow instantaneous code upgrades with zero delay. A compromised `Upgrader` key could instantly overwrite contract bytecode with malicious code, bypassing community inspection, audits, and emergency response procedures.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a configurable `timelock_delay_seconds` (e.g. default 48 hours / 34,560 ledgers) to `UpgradeabilityContract`
- [ ] In `UpgradeProposal`, record `eta` (earliest execution timestamp: `created_at + timelock_delay`)
- [ ] In `execute_upgrade`, enforce `env.ledger().timestamp() >= proposal.eta`
- [ ] Allow an emergency bypass only if contract is paused AND proposal has multi-admin consensus
- [ ] Add tests verifying that upgrades attempted prior to `eta` are rejected with `UpgradeError::TimelockNotExpired`

## Files to look at

- `contracts/upgradeability/src/lib.rs`
- `UPGRADEABILITY.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- Upgrades cannot be executed before the timelock window expires
- Proposed upgrades emit an on-chain event containing the target WASM hash and `eta`
- Tests cover timelock compliance and edge cases

---
**Skills:** Rust, Smart Contract Security  
**Estimated effort:** 2–3 days

issues.title: oracle: Prevent future timestamp manipulation and implement multi-source median aggregation
issues.body:
In `contracts/oracle-contract/src/lib.rs` (lines 125–130), `submit_price` validates staleness with:

```rust
let current_time = env.ledger().timestamp();
let staleness_window = storage::get_staleness_window(&env);
if current_time > timestamp + staleness_window {
    return Err(OracleError::SubmissionStale);
}
```

This check only checks if the submission is in the past. It never checks if `timestamp > current_time`. Furthermore, `get_latest_price` returns the single most recent price from whichever submitter posted last, with no medianization or multi-submitter consensus.

## Why this matters

- A rogue or compromised submitter could submit a timestamp far in the future (`u64::MAX` or days ahead), locking that price in as "fresh" indefinitely and bypassing future updates.
- Trusting a single submitter without a median or quorum creates a single point of failure for price feeds used by aid disbursement and rebalancing logic.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a maximum future skew check: reject submissions where `timestamp > current_time + MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECS` (e.g., 60 seconds)
- [ ] Prevent integer overflow on `timestamp.checked_add(staleness_window)`
- [ ] Implement multi-submitter median aggregation: track active submissions from distinct authorized submitters and compute the median when queried
- [ ] Require a minimum quorum of active submitters before a feed is considered valid
- [ ] Add comprehensive tests in `contracts/oracle-contract/src/tests.rs` for future timestamps and median calculations

## Files to look at

- `contracts/oracle-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/oracle-contract/src/storage.rs`
- `contracts/oracle-contract/src/tests.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Submissions with timestamps beyond permissible future skew are rejected
- Feeds require minimum submitter quorum and compute median prices
- Tests assert resilient pricing even if one submitter posts an outlier price

---
**Skills:** Rust, Oracle Design, Statistical Aggregation  
**Estimated effort:** 3–5 days

issues.title: nft-marketplace: Modularize 2,500-line monolithic `lib.rs` and isolate test harness
issues.body:
`contracts/nft-marketplace/src/lib.rs` is 2,533 lines long and contains all data types, error enums, storage helpers, market business logic, and ~850 lines of test code in a single file.

Additionally, line 22 contains `extern crate std;` at the root module without a `#[cfg(test)]` attribute, which conflicts with pure `no_std` compilation on Wasm targets.

## Why this matters

Every other contract crate (`aid-contract`, `oracle-contract`, `rebalancer-contract`) adheres to a clean modular architecture: separate `errors.rs`, `events.rs`, `storage.rs`, `types.rs`, `lib.rs`, and `tests.rs`. The 2,500-line monolithic file in `nft-marketplace` makes code review, maintenance, and audit significantly harder, and risks breaking `wasm32-unknown-unknown` builds due to unconditional `extern crate std;`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Guard `extern crate std;` with `#[cfg(test)]`
- [ ] Extract error codes into `contracts/nft-marketplace/src/errors.rs`
- [ ] Extract contract types into `contracts/nft-marketplace/src/types.rs`
- [ ] Extract storage keys and getters/setters into `contracts/nft-marketplace/src/storage.rs`
- [ ] Move test suite (lines 1680–2533) into `contracts/nft-marketplace/src/tests.rs`
- [ ] Keep `lib.rs` focused on public contract entry points
- [ ] Ensure `cargo test -p nft-marketplace` passes

## Files to look at

- `contracts/nft-marketplace/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/ (as architectural reference)`

## Acceptance criteria

- Crate is split into clean, modular sub-files
- No unqualified `extern crate std;` in production code
- All existing marketplace tests pass unchanged

---
**Skills:** Rust, Refactoring  
**Estimated effort:** 1 day

issues.title: payments: Multi-token support and token whitelist for payment gateway
issues.body:
In `contracts/payments-contract/src/lib.rs`, the payment contract only supports a single token specified at deployment:

```rust
instance_set(&env, &TOKEN, &token);
```

All deposit, withdrawal, and escrow methods implicitly assume this single token address.

## Why this matters

Trellis humanitarian aid programs accept and disburse funds in multiple assets: Stellar Lumens (native XLM), stablecoins (USDC, EURC), and local digital currencies. Restricting the payments contract to a single token requires deploying a separate contract instance for every token, fragmenting liquidity and complicating routing.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement an admin-managed token whitelist: `add_supported_token(token: Address)` / `remove_supported_token(token: Address)`
- [ ] Add `token: Address` parameter to `deposit`, `withdraw`, `create_escrow`, and `batch_pay`
- [ ] Track internal balances per `(user, token)` pair rather than flat user keys
- [ ] Ensure non-whitelisted tokens are rejected with `Error::PaymentTokenNotSupported`
- [ ] Update `contracts/payments-contract/src/test.rs` to test multi-token deposits and escrows

## Files to look at

- `contracts/payments-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/payments-contract/src/test.rs`
- `shared/src/payments.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Contract supports depositing, holding, and withdrawing multiple distinct SAC tokens
- Non-whitelisted tokens cannot be deposited
- Token balances are completely isolated across accounts and assets

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Token SDK  
**Estimated effort:** 2–3 days

issues.title: aid-contract: Implement public paginated query endpoints for donor and recipient aid history
issues.body:
In `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs`, `AidContract` defines `types::AidPage` and has an internal pagination helper `paginate` on line 487 annotated with `#[allow(dead_code)]`.

However, `AidContract` only exposes `get_aid(aid_id)` and `get_aid_latest(aid_id)`. There are no public functions for querying aid records by donor or recipient.

## Why this matters

Donors and recipients interacting with the Trellis web frontend or mobile app cannot discover what aids they have created or can claim directly from the contract. They are forced to rely entirely on off-chain indexers, which compromises decentralization and fails if indexers are down or out of sync.

## Tasks

- [ ] Maintain indexed ID lists per donor (`DataKey::DonorAids(Address) -> Vec<u64>`) and per recipient (`DataKey::RecipientAids(Address) -> Vec<u64>`)
- [ ] Implement public entry point: `pub fn list_aids_by_donor(env: Env, donor: Address, cursor: u32, limit: u32) -> AidPage`
- [ ] Implement public entry point: `pub fn list_aids_by_recipient(env: Env, recipient: Address, cursor: u32, limit: u32) -> AidPage`
- [ ] Enforce max query limit (`MAX_QUERY_LIMIT = 50`) to bound execution cost
- [ ] Add unit tests verifying pagination cursors, empty results, and multi-page traversals

## Files to look at

- `contracts/aid-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/storage.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/types.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/tests.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Frontends and wallets can paginate aids for any donor or recipient directly on-chain
- Paginating past the last page returns an empty list and `next_cursor: None`
- Unit tests verify forward progress and bound limits

---
**Skills:** Rust, API Design  
**Estimated effort:** 1–2 days

issues.title: rebalancer: Propagate strategy execution results and trade receipts to caller in `rebalance`
issues.body:
In `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/lib.rs` (lines 65–73):

```rust
if !dry_run {
    let _execution_result = execute_strategy(&env, &strategy, &trades);
    // TODO: In Phase 3.2+, capture execution details from result
}

let result = SimulationResult {
    expected_fees: total_fees,
    expected_slippage: total_slippage,
};
```

The result of `execute_strategy` is explicitly discarded with `let _execution_result`, and the contract returns `SimulationResult` even on live execution.

## Why this matters

Callers executing a multi-asset portfolio rebalance have no visibility into what happened during trade execution. They cannot see which trades succeeded, which failed, what actual fees were incurred, or what execution price was achieved. Live execution behaves identically to dry-run from the caller's perspective.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define an `ExecutionReport` contracttype containing: `total_fees`, `actual_slippage`, `trades_executed: u32`, `trades_failed: u32`, and individual trade statuses
- [ ] Return `ExecutionReport` from `execute_strategy` and propagate it through `rebalance`
- [ ] If any trade in a strategy fails, report the specific failure code without silently discarding the error
- [ ] Add tests in `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/tests.rs` asserting the details of the returned execution report

## Files to look at

- `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/strategy_executor.rs`
- `contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/tests.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- `MultiAssetRebalancer::rebalance` returns a comprehensive execution report with trade receipts
- Partial or total trade failures are surfaced to the caller
- Unit tests verify accurate report generation for both dry-run and live execution

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban  
**Estimated effort:** 2–3 days

issues.title: treasury: Add multi-token treasury vaults with per-asset category accounting
issues.body:
In `contracts/treasury-contract/src/lib.rs`, category balances are tracked using a two-element tuple key:

```rust
const BALANCE: Symbol = symbol_short!("cat_bal");
let key = (BALANCE, category.clone());
let balance: i128 = env.storage().instance().get(&key).unwrap_or(0);
```

There is no token address component in the storage key.

## Why this matters

If the treasury is funded with multiple tokens (e.g., 50,000 USDC and 100,000 XLM), depositing both into the `reserve` category will collapse both amounts into the same integer counter. Withdrawing 5,000 USDC would deduct from the combined total, corrupting the financial accounting of every asset held by the treasury. Treasury funds must be strictly segregated by both category and token address.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update balance storage key to a three-element tuple: `(BALANCE, token_address, category)`
- [ ] Update `deposit`, `withdraw`, `emergency_withdraw`, and `distribute_reward` to accept `token: Address`
- [ ] Validate that all balance checks and updates occur strictly per-asset
- [ ] Update `category_balance(token: Address, category: Symbol) -> i128`
- [ ] Update events to include the token address
- [ ] Add multi-asset isolation tests in `contracts/treasury-contract/src/test.rs`

## Files to look at

- `contracts/treasury-contract/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/treasury-contract/src/test.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

issues.title: upgradeability: Implement state migration dry-run and storage layout validation
issues.body:
In `contracts/upgradeability/src/lib.rs` (lines 69–70), the error `UpgradeError::StorageIncompatible` is declared, but there is no mechanism to validate storage layout compatibility before an upgrade is applied.

Currently, `execute_upgrade` invokes `env.deployer().update_current_contract_wasm()` and calls the migration hook without any pre-flight verification that existing persistent data is parseable by the new contract code.

## Why this matters

In Soroban, if an upgraded contract changes the layout of a `contracttype` struct or modifies enum discriminants, reads of previously stored records will immediately panic upon deserialization. Without a dry-run check, an incompatible WASM upgrade can permanently corrupt contract storage and lock funds irreversibly.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define a standard `MigrationHook` interface requiring a `validate_storage(&env, target: Address) -> Result<(), Error>` method
- [ ] In `propose_upgrade`, execute the validation hook in dry-run mode to sample existing storage keys and ensure they deserialize correctly
- [ ] Require the migration hook to verify critical protocol invariants (e.g. total balances equal token reserves)
- [ ] Add upgrade simulation tests in `testing/src/upgrade.rs` simulating a breaking schema change and confirming the upgrade is rejected

## Files to look at

- `contracts/upgradeability/src/lib.rs`
- `testing/src/upgrade.rs`
- `docs/MIGRATION_SAFETY.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- Incompatible WASM upgrades that break stored struct deserialization fail during validation
- Storage verification runs before bytecode is swapped
- Test harness demonstrates rejection of incompatible layout changes

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Serialization, Formal Verification  
**Estimated effort:** 3–4 days

issues.title: testing: Add property-based fuzz tests for basis-point fee and referral calculations
issues.body:
The Trellis protocol relies heavily on basis-point calculations across several contracts:
- Referral multi-tier commissions (`contracts/referral-contract/src/lib.rs`)
- Payment gateway fees (`contracts/payments-contract/src/lib.rs`)
- Rebalancer fee calculations (`contracts/rebalancer-contract/src/fee_calculator.rs`)
- NFT marketplace creator royalties (`contracts/nft-marketplace/src/lib.rs`)

While `shared/src/math.rs` provides `bps_of`, current unit tests only exercise standard round numbers (e.g. 1000 tokens at 500 BPS).

## Why this matters

DeFi and escrow protocols are frequently exploited or drained by rounding manipulation, off-by-one errors on fractional cents, and arithmetic overflow at boundary numbers ($2^{127}-1$). Without property-based fuzz testing across extreme ranges, dust leaks or transaction failure edges remain undiscovered.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create property-based test harness in `testing/src/fuzzing.rs` using `proptest` or `quickcheck`
- [ ] Test invariant: `sum(tier_commissions) <= base_amount` for all possible tier counts and BPS configurations
- [ ] Test invariant: fee calculation never exceeds principal amount (`fee <= amount`)
- [ ] Test boundary values: `amount = 0`, `amount = 1`, `amount = i128::MAX`, `bps = 0`, `bps = 10_000`
- [ ] Verify that no possible input generates an uncontrolled panic or overflow

## Files to look at

- `testing/src/fuzzing.rs`
- `shared/src/math.rs`
- `contracts/referral-contract/src/lib.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Property tests run 10,000+ random test cases without overflow or invariant violation
- Rounding behavior is documented and verified deterministic
- Fuzz tests run in CI

---
**Skills:** Rust, Property-based Testing, Arithmetic Safety  
**Estimated effort:** 2 days

issues.title: governance: Implement proposal expiration and cancellation mechanisms
issues.body:
In `contracts/governance-contract/src/lib.rs` (lines 113–120), `Proposal` defines:

```rust
pub struct Proposal {
    pub id: u64,
    pub proposer: Address,
    pub action: ProposalAction,
    pub approval_count: u32,
    pub status: ProposalStatus,
    pub created_at: u64,
}
```

Proposals only have two states: `Pending` and `Executed`. There is no expiration timestamp, and no function exists for a proposer or admin to cancel an obsolete or erroneous proposal.

## Why this matters

If an admin proposes a parameter change that later turns out to be flawed or superseded by network conditions, that proposal remains `Pending` forever in contract storage. Months later, if administrative membership changes or another admin inadvertently approves it, the stale proposal can be executed, enacting obsolete parameters.

## Tasks

- [ ] Extend `ProposalStatus` with `Cancelled` and `Expired` variants
- [ ] Add `expires_at: u64` to `Proposal` (e.g., `created_at + PROPOSAL_LIFETIME`)
- [ ] In `approve` and `execute`, reject proposals where `env.ledger().timestamp() > proposal.expires_at` with `Error::ProposalExpired`
- [ ] Implement `pub fn cancel(env: Env, caller: Address, proposal_id: u64) -> Result<(), Error>` callable by the original proposer or super-admin
- [ ] Add tests in `contracts/governance-contract/src/lib.rs` covering proposal expiration and cancellation

## Files to look at

- `contracts/governance-contract/src/lib.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Expired proposals cannot be approved or executed
- Proposers can cancel their own pending proposals prior to execution
- All state transitions emit corresponding governance events

---
**Skills:** Rust, Governance Contract Logic  
**Estimated effort:** 1–2 days

issues.title: shared: Standardize TTL extension and renewal helpers across all contract persistent writes
issues.body:
Stellar Soroban contracts require periodic TTL (Time To Live) extension on all persistent storage entries to prevent ledger archival. In `shared/src/storage.rs`, constants `PERSISTENT_BUMP_AMOUNT` (120,960 ledgers) and `PERSISTENT_TTL_THRESHOLD` are defined.

However, individual contracts (`contracts/aid-contract/src/storage.rs`, `contracts/oracle-contract/src/storage.rs`, `shared/src/migration.rs`) implement custom or inconsistent TTL bump logic, and several write paths omit `extend_ttl` altogether.

## Why this matters

If an aid record, oracle submission, or referral registration is written without extending its TTL, or if reads don't refresh the threshold, entries can expire and be archived by the network after ~7 days of inactivity. An archived aid record prevents donors and recipients from claiming or refunding funds.

## Tasks

- [ ] Audit all `env.storage().persistent().set(...)` calls across all crates in `contracts/` and `shared/`
- [ ] Standardize all persistent writes to use `shared::storage::persistent_set` which automatically invokes `extend_ttl`
- [ ] Ensure query paths that access critical state call `shared::storage::persistent_get` to refresh the TTL
- [ ] Document explicit TTL renewal rules in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`
- [ ] Add test cases verifying that entry TTL is bumped upon read and write

## Files to look at

- `shared/src/storage.rs`
- `contracts/aid-contract/src/storage.rs`
- `contracts/oracle-contract/src/storage.rs`
- `shared/src/migration.rs`

## Acceptance criteria

- Every persistent entry write and read uses standardized TTL helpers
- No raw un-bumped persistent sets remain in production contract crates
- Tests verify TTL threshold extension on active records

---
**Skills:** Rust, Soroban Storage Model  
**Estimated effort:** 2 days

issues.title: scripts: Add deployment and cross-contract initialization validation smoke-test script for testnet
issues.body:
`scripts/deploy.sh` and `scripts/initialize.sh` exist to compile and deploy contracts to Stellar testnet. However, there is no verification or smoke-test script that validates whether the deployed contracts are correctly wired together.

## Why this matters

The Trellis contract architecture is interdependent:
- `AidContract` needs the `TreasuryContract` address and token address
- `ReferralContract` needs the `TreasuryContract` address
- `TreasuryContract` must register the `ReferralContract` as authorized for `distribute_reward`
- `GovernanceContract` needs threshold admins registered
- `RegistryContract` must index all current contract addresses

A misconfigured or omitted step in `scripts/initialize.sh` leaves the system in a broken state where claims or payouts fail on-chain.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `scripts/verify-deployment.sh` (and Windows equivalent or Node.js runner)
- [ ] Read deployed contract addresses from `DEPLOYMENTS.md` or deployment output JSON
- [ ] Query each contract's getters to verify:
  - `AidContract::get_treasury` matches deployed Treasury
  - `TreasuryContract::referral_contract` matches deployed Referral
  - `ReferralContract::get_treasury` matches deployed Treasury
  - `RegistryContract` has entries for all deployed contracts
- [ ] Execute a zero-value test simulation call to confirm contract invocation rights
- [ ] Document usage in `docs/RUNBOOK.md`

## Files to look at

- `scripts/deploy.sh`
- `scripts/initialize.sh`
- `DEPLOYMENTS.md`
- `docs/RUNBOOK.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- Smoke-test script validates all contract linkages in a single command
- Clear pass/fail report output for maintainers deploying to testnet
- Detects and flags any missing or mismatched contract addresses

---
**Skills:** Bash / Shell, Soroban CLI, DevOps  
**Estimated effort:** 1 day
